Definition: from a primary θέρω (to heat); properly, heat, i.e. summer:--summer.
BiblicalUsage: théros is the word for summer. In Matthew 24:32, ye know that summer is nigh, and it appears again in Mark 13:28.
TheologicalSignificance: A fig tree budding to tell summer is near teaches me to read the signs God gives instead of pretending I cannot see them.
